messages:
Check that a patch's "value" is a JSON value, all the way down

A JSON Patch document is a JSON document (RFC 6902 § 3), so the "value"
member of an "add", "replace" or "test" holds a JSON value. readValue
only refused one that was undefined at the top, so everything else went
through unexamined and applyPatch wrote it into the document: an object
member that was undefined, NaN, an infinity, a function, a symbol, a
bigint, a hole in an array, or a Date or a Map that cloneJson copied
down to an empty object. None of those survive JSON.stringify as what
they were, so the document the caller got back was no longer JSON, and a
"test" against such a value failed with a message that showed the two
values as equal. A value containing itself did not even fail as a patch
error: it recursed until the stack ran out.

findNonJsonValue walks a value and reports the first part of it that the
data model does not have, with the reference tokens that lead there, so
the operation is now rejected with 'invalid-patch' and an error that
names the place inside "value". Members an operation does not define are
still ignored, whatever they hold.
